schema_info.ce_logic: Positive CE = control in place = adds to Total_CE = lowers risk

A1_1.text: What is the primary function of the AI system?

A1_2.text: What version of the AI solution does this FAIRA assessment apply to?

A1_3.text: Which AI features or capabilities does the system include?

A1_4.text: What decisions will be addressed by the AI functionality?

A1_5.text: What tangible benefits does this AI solution provide?

A1_6.text: Can the AI solution convert decisions into actions without human intervention?
A1_6.scoring_notes: If Yes: AutonomyFactor = +3 applies to Likelihood. Each selected action adds its Likelihood and Impact modifiers.

A1_7.text: What type of AI model or technique is used?

A1_8.text: What is the source of the AI solution?

A1_9.text: How does the AI solution integrate with other systems?

A2_1.text: How are AI use inputs tracked and recorded?
A2_1.scoring_notes: Each selected option adds to CE. 'No inputs tracked or recorded' should be flagged as a risk.

A2_2.text: Does the AI require data from the digital or physical environment?

Yes.notes: A2.2 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, selections increase Impact/Likelihood based on data sensitivity and exposure pathways. User-limiting controls and traceability mechanisms improve Control Effectiveness.

A2_3.text: What safeguards exist to detect and handle corrupted, missing, or out-of-range data inputs?
A2_3.scoring_notes: Each safeguard option reduces likelihood. 'No safeguards identified' increases risk and should be flagged.

A2_4.text: What data does the AI solution use?

A2_5.text: Rate the quality of the input data (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High):
A2_5.scoring_notes: High quality (rating=5) lowers risk. Poor quality (rating=1) raises likelihood. DataQualityFactor ranges from +1 (perfect quality) to +5 (very poor quality).

A2_6.text: What is the Business Impact Level (BIL) of the input data?

A2_7.text: Does the solution use regulated or sensitive data?
A2_7.scoring_notes: If Yes: base +2 Impact. Each selected regulated data type adds its Impact and Likelihood modifiers.

A2_8.text: Does the solution require user inputs to operate?
A2_8.scoring_notes: Selecting YES does not add modifiers itself. Only when specific input types are selected does scoring occur.

A3_1.text: How does the system interface with humans?

A3_2.text: What expertise is required to use the AI solution? (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High):
A3_2.scoring_notes: High expertise required (rating=5) → +2. Medium (rating=3) → 0. Low expertise required (rating=1) → -2. Lower expertise requirements reduce risk.

A3_3.text: Who will be impacted by the AI system?
A3_3.scoring_notes: Each selected group adds to Impact cumulatively.

A3_4.text: How will impacted parties be informed of AI use?
A3_4.scoring_notes: Each notification method adds to Control Effectiveness. 'No planned notifications' should be flagged as a risk.

A3_5.text: A3.5(a) What are the expected impacts of this AI solution on staff?
A3_5.scoring_notes: Part (a): Select all applicable staff impacts. Part (b): Rate overall severity. Final impact is base impact multiplied by severity.

A3_6.text: A3.6(a) How will each impacted group be affected?
A3_6.scoring_notes: Part (a): Select all applicable group impacts. Part (b): Rate severity (1=Minor, 2=Moderate, 3=Major). Final impact is sum of modifiers multiplied by severity.

A4_1.text: What are the primary outputs of the AI system?

A4_2.text: Are outputs sent to external systems without human review?

A4_3.text: What is the Business Impact Level (BIL) of the outputs?

A4_4.text: How are AI outputs tracked and recorded?
A4_4.scoring_notes: Each tracking method adds to Control Effectiveness. 'Not currently tracked' should be flagged as a risk.

A4_5.text: Could any AI outputs allow unauthorised access to information?
A4_5.scoring_notes: Each selected risk applies both Impact and Likelihood modifiers. Risks are cumulative.

A4_6.text: Do outputs involve data regulated by law?
A4_6.scoring_notes: If Yes: select applicable regulated data types. Each selected data type adds to Impact cumulatively.

A4_7.text: Do outputs contain personally identifiable information (PII)? If yes, who can access it?

Yes.notes: A4.7 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, Impact and Likelihood increase based on PII sensitivity and access scope. Strong access controls improve Control Effectiveness.

access_controls.label: Access controls for PII outputs
access_controls.notes: Controls contribute to Control Effectiveness. If controls are 'Not in place / unknown', Likelihood increases.

A4_8.text: Do any AI outputs directly trigger actions with legal or regulatory effect?

Yes.notes: A4.8 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, Impact is elevated due to legal/regulatory consequences. Likelihood increases when actions are automated without human review, when review/appeal is absent, or when the legal basis is unclear. Traceability and contestability mechanisms improve Control Effectiveness.

A5_1.text: Who is accountable for decisions made using this system?
A5_1.scoring_notes: Select the primary accountability role. Higher-level oversight provides stronger governance.

A5_10.text: Are there sector-specific frameworks, laws, or regulatory obligations that apply to this AI solution?

other.label: Other regulations, obligations, or frameworks (optional)
other.notes: Free-text field with default CE -1. Can be LLM-classified later for adjustment if needed.

A5_10.scoring_notes: Multi-part question. All modifiers only apply if 'Yes' is selected. Each subsection is cumulative. Strong controls from critical infrastructure, child protection, and law enforcement obligations.

A5_11.text: Where will this AI solution be deployed?
A5_11.scoring_notes: Single select - only ONE deployment location applies. Wider deployment increases likelihood of risk exposure but also may come with better controls. Citizen-facing and multi-channel deployments have highest risk exposure but strongest control requirements.

A5_2.text: Are AI inputs, outputs, and/or decisions logged or recorded?

No.notes: Absence of logging reduces traceability and the ability to investigate outcomes; increases likelihood of undetected issues.

Yes.notes: A5.2 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, traceability and governance assurance are strengthened. Specific selections adjust likelihood and control effectiveness based on auditability, retention, and access scope.

logged_items.label: What is logged/recorded
logged_items.notes: Logging more artefacts increases traceability and assurance value.

logging_mechanisms.label: Logging mechanisms
logging_mechanisms.notes: Dedicated audit logs and centralised logging improve control effectiveness; manual-only records increase likelihood of gaps.

retention.label: Retention period
retention.notes: Short or unknown retention increases likelihood that evidence will be unavailable for investigation.

access_scope.label: Access scope
access_scope.notes: Appropriate restriction and audit access supports assurance; overly broad or unknown access increases likelihood of misuse.

A5_3.text: What monitoring and evaluation processes are in place?
A5_3.scoring_notes: Each monitoring and evaluation process adds to Control Effectiveness. Multiple processes indicate comprehensive oversight.

A5_4.text: How frequently will monitoring and evaluation occur?
A5_4.scoring_notes: More frequent monitoring provides stronger control effectiveness.

A5_5.text: Has the AI solution been subject to independent review?

A5_6.text: Who is responsible for monitoring and evaluation?
A5_6.scoring_notes: Select the primary role responsible for monitoring and evaluation.

A5_7.text: How are stakeholders engaged in monitoring and evaluation?

A5_8.text: How are undesirable or harmful results detected?

A5_9.text: Which values and principles informed the AI solution's design?

B1_2.text: What negative impacts could the AI system create?
B1_2.scoring_notes: Multiple selections are cumulative. Safety risks have the highest impact modifier.

B1_3.text: Could the AI system affect employee employment or job roles?
B1_3.scoring_notes: Single select - only ONE option applies. 'Unknown' reflects uncertainty about employment impacts.

B2_1.text: Has a Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) been completed?
B2_1.scoring_notes: Completing an HRIA improves control effectiveness. Not completing one increases risk exposure.

B2_2.text: Rate the AI system's impact on the following dimensions:
B2_2.scoring_notes: Each category is rated independently. Only ONE rating per category applies. All three ratings are cumulative. Positive impacts reduce risk, negative impacts increase it significantly.

B2_3.text: Were diverse perspectives included in the AI system's design and development?
B2_3.scoring_notes: Two-part question. If 'No', Impact +2. If 'Yes', Impact -2 PLUS each selected perspective adds -0.5. 'Other' option available but has no additional score modifier.

B3_1.text: Has bias testing been conducted on the AI system?
B3_1.scoring_notes: Two-part question. If 'No', Impact +2. If 'Yes', Impact -2 PLUS each selected testing method adds -1. 'Informal or ad-hoc checks only' should be flagged as a risk despite the -1 modifier, as it indicates lack of formal testing.

B3_2.text: Could the AI system discriminate against specific groups?
B3_2.scoring_notes: Three-option question. If 'No', Impact 0. If 'Unknown', Impact +2 only. If 'Yes', Impact +3 PLUS each selected group adds +1. This identifies potential discrimination risks.

B4_1.text: Has a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) been completed?
B4_1.scoring_notes: Completing a PIA improves control effectiveness. Not completing one increases risk exposure.

B4_2.text: Does the AI system use personal information?
B4_2.scoring_notes: Two-part question. If 'No', Impact 0. If 'Yes', Impact +2 PLUS each selected PI type adds its modifier. Health, Financial, and Biometric data carry highest impact.

B4_3.text: What security measures are in place to protect personal information?
B4_3.scoring_notes: Multiple selections are cumulative. Each security measure improves control effectiveness.

B5_1.text: Has the system been tested for reliability?
B5_1.scoring_notes: Two-part question. If 'No', CE 0 only. If 'Yes', CE 0 but unlocks rating scale (1-5). Rating reflects robustness of testing: 1 = Minimal/ad hoc, 5 = Comprehensive/formal. Higher ratings improve control effectiveness more.

B5_2.text: Is there a process to disengage the system if issues arise?
B5_2.scoring_notes: Having a disengagement mechanism improves control effectiveness. Lacking one increases risk exposure.

B5_3.text: Does the AI system operate in a high-risk environment?
B5_3.scoring_notes: Two-part question with dual metrics. If 'No', Impact 0 and Likelihood 0 only. If 'Yes', unlocks environment options. Each selected environment applies both Impact and Likelihood modifiers. Democratic processes carry the highest impact.

B6_1.text: How transparent is the AI solution's operation? (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High)
B6_1.scoring_notes: Rating scale 1-5. Higher transparency improves control effectiveness. Rating 1 (Very Low) has no effect, Rating 5 (Very High) provides strongest control benefit.

B6_2.text: Can the system explain its outputs or decisions? (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High)
B6_2.scoring_notes: Rating scale 1-5. Higher explainability improves control effectiveness. Rating 1 (Very Low) has no effect, Rating 5 (Very High) provides strongest control benefit.

B6_3.text: Are users and/or affected individuals informed that AI is being used?

No.notes: No disclosure increases the likelihood of misunderstanding, inappropriate reliance, and complaints/escalations.

Yes.notes: B6.3 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, transparency improves (negative CE). Specific disclosure quality affects both CE and Likelihood.

audience.label: Who is informed
audience.notes: Informing affected individuals provides the strongest transparency benefit.

methods.label: How they are informed
methods.notes: Direct and contextual disclosures provide stronger transparency benefit than passive policy-only disclosures.

timing.label: When they are informed
timing.notes: Earlier disclosure improves transparency; after-the-fact disclosure increases likelihood of dissatisfaction and disputes.

information_provided.label: What information is provided
information_provided.notes: Providing limitations and contest/review pathways materially improves transparency outcomes.

B6_4.text: Can meaningful explanations of AI-supported outcomes be provided to users and/or affected individuals?

No.notes: If meaningful explanations are not available, there is an increased likelihood of misunderstanding, inappropriate reliance, and disputes.

Yes.notes: B6.4 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, explainability improves (negative CE). The quality, timing, and accessibility of explanations influences both CE and Likelihood.

audience.label: Who can receive explanations
audience.notes: Providing explanations to affected individuals provides the strongest explainability benefit.

explanation_methods.label: How explanations are provided
explanation_methods.notes: Contextual explanations at the point of output provide stronger explainability than passive documentation-only approaches.

timing.label: When explanations are available
timing.notes: Earlier and point-of-output explainability improves transparency; deferring to formal review increases likelihood of friction and disputes.

explanation_content.label: What explanations include
explanation_content.notes: Including key factors and uncertainty indicators materially improves explainability quality.

accessibility.label: Accessibility to non-technical audiences
accessibility.notes: Plain language explanations reduce misunderstanding and support effective challenge/review pathways.

limitations_disclosed.label: Limitations/uncertainty communicated
limitations_disclosed.notes: Communicating limitations supports appropriate reliance and reduces likelihood of harm from misinterpretation.

B7_1.text: Is there a defined process for challenging or reviewing AI-supported outcomes?

No.notes: Absence of a defined contestability process increases the likelihood of unaddressed errors, disputes, and loss of trust.

Yes.notes: B7.1 is a Yes/No gate. If Yes, contestability improves. The strength of contestability depends on who can initiate review, how it is triggered, what evidence supports it, and whether outcomes can be changed.

initiators.label: Who can initiate a challenge or review
initiators.notes: Allowing affected individuals to initiate review provides the strongest contestability signal.

channels.label: How a challenge or review can be initiated
channels.notes: Formalised and trackable channels improve contestability and auditability.

review_process.label: Review process available
review_process.notes: A meaningful review process requires human review and the ability to intervene.

review_inputs.label: Information supporting review
review_inputs.notes: Review inputs improve the ability to investigate and correct outcomes.

outcome_change.label: Can outcomes be changed following review?
outcome_change.notes: Contestability is materially weaker if outcomes cannot be changed.

B7_2.text: How quickly can decisions be challenged or reviewed?

B8_2.text: Have roles and responsibilities for AI governance been established?

B8_3.text: Have staff been trained on AI governance and ethical use?

B8_4.text: Are there safeguards against overreliance on AI outputs?
